rationale: 1 Peter 3:6 (BSB) names both people and the word: 'just as Sarah obeyed Abraham and called him lord.' The only place in Genesis where Sarah calls Abraham by that title is her laugh in 18:12, which the BSB renders 'my master is old'; the Septuagint has 'ὁ δὲ κύριός μου πρεσβύτερος' (Brenton: 'and my lord is old'), and 1 Peter's Greek is 'κύριον αὐτὸν καλοῦσα', the same noun. So the English of this app's BSB hides a link the Greek shows plainly. Commentators on both verses connect them: Barnes, Jamieson-Fausset-Brown, Gill, Bengel and the Pulpit Commentary on 1 Peter 3:6 cite Genesis 18:12, and Benson, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary on Genesis 18:12 cite 1 Peter 3:6. Two named readers point out how narrow the base is. The Expositor's Greek Testament calls 18:12 'The only evidence that can be adduced from the O.T. narrative' and adds that the context 'excludes any hope in God'; the Cambridge Bible on 1 Peter 3:6 says 'the history of Genesis supplies no such instance in act' and so Peter 'saw in her use of "my lord"' a representative utterance. Ellicott notes that Sarah says it to herself, not to Abraham. Graded explicit_reference at explicit because 1 Peter names Sarah, Abraham, and the title she used. The grade measures how certain the reference is. It does not decide how 1 Peter 3:1-7 applies to marriage today, which traditions dispute (see the lesson's Positions).
